items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Seattle, New York City
items.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost. - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load. - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers. - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested. - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back. - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works. - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice. - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure. - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them. - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count. - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down. - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing). - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it. - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter. - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets. - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF. - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar. - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls. - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch. - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar). - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

items.title: Talent Sourcer, Tech
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? Cohere is in a unique and exciting position to grow our go-to-market teams globally! We are expanding our Talent Team and are looking for creative, high-performing talent sourcers who are eager to take on a new challenge as we are in the early stages of building the Talent Acquisition function. In this role, you will master a new domain of sourcing, source world-class technical talent, and influence the scaling of a high-growth Canadian tech company. If you consider yourself resilient, collaborative, influential, and a lifelong learner with an established network, we’d love to hear from you! Please Note: We have offices in Toronto, San Francisco, and London but embrace being remote-first! As a Talent Sourcer, you will: - Build, own, and nurture a strong pipeline of world-class business talent across Engineering and Research roles. - Deliver a world-class recruiting experience that reflects Cohere's premium brand - Partner with hiring managers and talent partners to find and engage passive talent through creative sourcing methods - Maintain deep market intelligence on technical talent trends and competitive landscape - Manage comprehensive recruiting funnels in our ATS, updating progress and analytics regularly - Develop creative, proactive sourcing approaches to optimize the top of the funnel for business roles - Cultivate relationships with established networks across business communities and industry leaders - Identify and own additional high-impact talent projects as they emerge Who you are: - You have 5+ years of experience sourcing for technical roles across engineering and research in markets like EMEA/US etc. - You have a proven track record of sourcing candidates in high-growth and a high-bar environments (startup, technology, AI experience strongly preferred) - You bring an established, high-profile network in business communities - You're a creative problem solver who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments - You're a natural influencer with exceptional relationship-building skills - You leverage data and analytics to drive sourcing decisions and measure effectiveness - You're passionate about diversity, equity, and building inclusive business teams - You have a strategic mindset with the ability to see beyond immediate hiring needs Why Cohere - Impact: Shape the future of AI talent at a cutting-edge company. - Culture: Collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven. - Growth: Join a team scaling from 800 to 2000+ over 18 months. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Toronto, Seattle, New York City
items.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads. RESPONSIBILITIES - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure. - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs. - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints. - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet. - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run. - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention. - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply. - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE). - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is. - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load. - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++. - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM. - Slurm or other HPC schedulers. - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable. - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production. - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. At Robinhood, Quality Engineering (QE) is a critical function within our broader engineering organization. We serve as the final line of defense for product quality—empowering teams to ship confidently by embedding robust test strategies, running critical end-to-end checks, and maintaining automation systems that scale with our product velocity. Our mission is to uphold a high bar for customer experience, especially during P0 launches, through a mix of technical expertise, test execution, and cross-functional collaboration. As a Senior Quality Engineer, you will support high-impact product launches by designing test strategies, executing manual and automated testing, and partnering with our contractor team on regression test cycles. This role requires someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, cares deeply about the customer experience, and is eager to shape the test infrastructure behind Robinhood’s iOS, Android, and Web apps. This role is based in our New York City, New York office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Own the quality of new features, including test planning, execution, and feedback throughout the development cycle Define and implement test strategies for P0 product launches, including both frontend and backend validation Perform manual and automated testing, with a focus on end-to-end functionality Automate mobile/web E2E test cases Build test coverage that accurately reflects the user experience, including functional, regression, and exploratory testing What you bring Proven experience testing mobile (iOS/Android) and web applications in fast-paced product environments Strong understanding of quality assurance principles, test case development, and test execution Hands-on experience with UI automation tools such as Appium, Selenium, Playwright Comfort with scripting languages (e.g., Python, Java) and test infrastructure tools Familiarity with bug tracking (e.g., Jira) and test case management tools (e.g., TestRail) Excellent communication skills, user empathy, and a detail-oriented mindset What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. items.title: Motion Designer
items.description: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Role OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications. Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll help determine what a story needs visually, explore different approaches, and bring those ideas to life through thoughtful design and animation. This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and the ability to find a compelling visual approach when the brief is still taking shape. You’ll contribute to how OpenAI’s research is expressed in motion, developing original work and reusable approaches that help the team build on what it learns. In this role, you will: - Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to understand the ideas and identify how best to communicate them. - Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content. - Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story. - Take work from visual exploration, storyboards, and animatics through animation, compositing, and final delivery. - Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers, bringing a motion perspective into the creative process early. - Translate technical or abstract concepts into visual sequences that are accessible to a broad audience while preserving the meaning of the underlying work. - Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve. - Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners. - Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work. - A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution. - The ability to explore an open-ended brief, propose a clear creative direction, and refine it through collaboration. - Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows. - Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams. - A strong understanding of typography, composition, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling. - Experience making complex or unfamiliar subjects understandable through design and motion. - Experience working with subject matter experts and incorporating technical feedback without losing clarity or creative quality. - Curiosity about AI and research, and a willingness to learn enough about a subject to represent it thoughtfully. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. items.location_text: New York, New York, United States
items.description: Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge? This is a rare thing in ad sales: you’ll be KICK’s first Senior Client Partner in the US. There’s no book to inherit. You’ll map the region, choose where we start and decide how KICK goes to market with agencies and advertisers, with a real say in what the product becomes. What you’ll build with us: Open the US market for KICK and own the revenue number. You’ll go beyond the media buy, into sponsorships and branded integrations campaigns. This is a full-time opportunity based in New York. You’ll work from home, but you won’t be working alone. You’ll be out in the market with agencies and advertisers, and closely connected to our Australian and Serbian teams as we build KICK’s US presence together. Who is Easygo and KICK? Easygo is a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands, including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. These brands have a fierce global following, but our crew is employed directly by Easygo, and that’s where the real fun happens. KICK is our live streaming platform, built to put creators and their communities first. It gives content creators 95% of their streaming income and has redefined what a live streaming platform can be. KICK started as a disruptor challenging the status quo. Since launching in 2022, it has grown to more than 100 million accounts, and 81.7% of its audience is aged 18 to 34. Creators stream on KICK across gaming, talk shows, podcasts, IRL, sport and events. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast, and who are ready to Unify, Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact, and that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Own and deliver KICK’s US revenue across video, display and native inventory Open the holding groups and the advertisers behind them, building trusted relationships from planning teams up to C-level Lead data driven strategy and storytelling, translating complex performance data into clear insights, recommendations, and narratives that influence senior decision makers and unlock upsell and cross sell opportunities. Build KICK’s US commercial story, using the audience, category and data-led proof points that get us onto plans Negotiate annual trading agreements, master agreements and multi-year spend commitments Own the pipeline and forecast, and grow the region year on year through retention, share of wallet and new accounts Mentor the team as it grows, and set the standard for how KICK sells in the region, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Your track record: 9+ years in digital media sales, with a proven record of owning and delivering a holding group or regional revenue number Established relationships across US agency groups, independents and key advertisers Experience negotiating trading agreements and multi-year commitments, and presenting to senior agency and client stakeholders Working knowledge of programmatic (PMPs, programmatic guaranteed, and DSP and SSP mechanics) Familiarity with CRM and order management systems (Boostr is a plus) Comfort building without an established process, in a function and region that are both being built Bonus points if you also have: Experience with creator networks, streaming, live broadcasting, entertainment or gaming platforms Relationships with programmatic buyers and brand-direct advertisers Here are our benefits and perks: Sharpening your edge The ultimate sandbox. Exciting, on-the-job learning opportunities. 1 in 3 of our people level up their roles every year. If you deliver, you move. Competitive pay and bonus scheme Market-synced pay that respects your craft and location. Performance-based bonus recognition based on your impact (up to 20%). Help us build our crew and get paid for it with our high-value referral bonus. Because great people know great people. Other perks 18 weeks of paid parental leave for primary carers, so you can be there for the moments that matter. Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage. Matched 401(k) contributions, so your future grows alongside your career. We play fair. We hire fair. True to our value of ‘Play fair’ we always hire fair. Our work and our brands are fuelled by our diverse culture. We hire for talent and grit. But we never discriminate. Your race, religion, nationality, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital, veteran, or disability status won’t affect our hiring decision, or your trajectory here. Your work has impact, and that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. Build KICK’s EMEA commercial story, using the audience, category and data-led proof points that get us onto plans Negotiate annual trading agreements, master agreements and multi-year spend commitments Own the pipeline and forecast, and grow the region year on year through retention, share of wallet and new accounts Mentor the team as it grows, and set the standard for how KICK sells in the region, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement. items.title: Intelligence Systems Analyst
items.description: About the Team The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We also draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership. I2 Engineering works hand in hand with I2’s analysts and investigators, building tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish. Our tools help them make sense of vast and complex datasets, discover and measure on-platform and off-platform risk, and investigate severe misuse with greater speed, depth, and consistency. About the Role We are looking for an Intelligence Systems Analyst who wants to work alongside investigators to understand difficult cases, contribute to analysis, and build tools and workflows that help the team do more. As investigators pursue leads, assess risks, and determine what happened, you’ll see where better tools could help and build them. The role combines hands-on software and data work with meaningful participation in investigations. Depending on the problem, you might trace activity across internal systems, write a query or small application, prototype an AI-assisted workflow, improve how evidence is assembled, or turn an investigator’s recurring need into a durable product capability. You will work closely with engineers, analysts, investigators, and other subject matter experts. Success requires enough operational understanding to contribute meaningfully to an investigation and enough technical ownership to build solutions that remain useful after the immediate case is resolved. In this role, you will: - Work directly alongside investigators on complex cases, helping develop leads, analyze evidence, and identify useful technical approaches. - Build and maintain software, data workflows, and internal tools that accelerate investigations of potential high-severity misuse or harm. - Use Python, SQL, and internal data systems to gather, connect, and analyze information relevant to investigative work. - Apply OpenAI’s models to research, search, triage, synthesis, and evidence review in workflows that keep expert investigators informed and in control. - Turn recurring investigative bottlenecks into reliable tools, automation, and product capabilities that support multiple users and cases. - Prototype quickly when a new investigative question arises, then improve reliability, usability, and maintainability as requirements become clearer. - Respect the privacy, permissions, evidence-handling requirements, and operational safeguards that accompany sensitive investigative work. - Collaborate with teams across Applied, Safety Systems, Research, User Operations, and Strategy when their expertise or systems are needed. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Experience building and shipping software, internal tools, data workflows, or operational products. - Comfort working directly with investigators, analysts, or other subject matter experts in ambiguous or consequential situations. - Practical experience with Python, SQL, and structured or unstructured data. - The ability to investigate an unclear problem, follow evidence across systems, and turn what you learn into a practical next step. - Sound judgment about privacy, data access, evidence quality, and the consequences of getting an investigation wrong. - Interest in using AI systems to extend human investigative capability while keeping expert judgment central. - The flexibility to move between coding, analysis, investigative support, and close collaboration with technical and operational partners. Experience in trust and safety, security, intelligence, investigations, or related domains is helpful but not required. items.title: Marketing Technology & Operations Lead, APAC
items.description: ABOUT OPENAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company committed to ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of AI capabilities while prioritizing safety, responsible deployment, and human needs. Our mission requires a team that represents a diversity of perspectives, voices, and experiences. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an experienced JAPAC Marketing Operations Lead to build the operational foundations that connect regional B2B marketing activity to customer engagement, sales progression, and measurable business impact. This role serves as a critical bridge between global marketing and revenue operations and GEO B2B leaders, ensuring field leadership drives optimized customer journeys, measurement frameworks, and performance impact. It will deliver country level performance reporting and insights. Embedded in JAPAC’s GTM strategy, you will work closely with country marketing leads, GTM leaders, and Sales Operations to translate business priorities into a regional operations roadmap. You will represent JAPAC’s requirements with global Marketing Operations, ensuring that technology, data, and process decisions support local sales motions, customer journeys, and growth priorities. This is a hands-on role spanning the customer journey—from audience acquisition and database health through campaign execution, lead management, and performance reporting. You will combine technical fluency, analytical judgment, and strong cross-functional collaboration to help regional teams launch faster, improve follow-up, and understand what drives results. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the regional operations roadmap. Partner with JAPAC Marketing, GTM, and Sales Operations to consolidate country requirements, prioritize improvements against business goals, and represent regional needs in global MarkOps planning. - Manage regional marketing technology operations. Oversee the regional use of marketing automation, CRM, and event and webinar platforms. Work with global MarkOps and systems teams to troubleshoot issues, improve integrations, and validate changes across markets. - Build a healthier, more actionable database. Partner with GTM on priority-account and contact acquisition, enrichment, segmentation, and data quality. Improve opt-in coverage and marketability while maintaining appropriate consent and data-handling practices. - Own campaign setup, lead management, and sales handoffs. Set up and quality-check campaigns in marketing automation and CRM systems, including audience lists, registration forms, campaign tracking, and lead-capture workflows. Ensure leads from field events, webinars, and other campaigns enter the agreed qualification and routing processes. Work with Sales Operations, AEs, and SDRs to conduct regular reviews of untouched marketing-qualified leads (MQLs) and resolve routing or follow-up gaps. - Connect the customer journey. Work with regional marketers and global MarkOps to connect acquisition, engagement, nurture, and sales touchpoints, making relevant customer signals available to the teams that need to act on them. - Standardize campaign execution. Develop reusable templates, workflows, and quality checks that help field marketers launch campaigns quickly and consistently, with documented adaptations for local requirements. - Partner with Legal/Privacy and global MarkOps to embed market-specific data privacy and regulatory requirements across JAPAC into consent management, audience acquisition, campaign execution, and data handling. - Measure campaign performance and impact. Establish reliable reporting for field programs, local events, webinars, and account-based marketing. Apply shared measurement and attribution definitions to assess engagement, conversion, pipeline contribution, and ROI where the data supports it. - Enable regional teams. Train marketers on tools, campaign processes, data quality, and applicable privacy and compliance requirements. Provide practical support during JAPAC working hours and coordinate specialist guidance where needed. Partner with Sales Operations to jointly enable GTM teams on lead follow-up processes, ownership, and service-level agreements (SLAs). - Improve automation and operating efficiency. Identify repetitive work and partner with global teams to introduce dependable automation and AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual handoffs and improve execution. QUALIFICATIONS - 10+ years of experience in B2B marketing operations, marketing technology, revenue operations, or a closely related function. - Hands-on experience with marketing automation and CRM platforms, including Marketo and Salesforce, Adobe Experience Platform and familiarity with event or webinar technology. - Demonstrated experience improving database quality, segmentation, lead lifecycle processes, scoring, routing, and marketing-to-sales handoffs. - Strong analytical skills, with experience in campaign reporting, funnel analysis, attribution, and translating findings into operational improvements. - Experience supporting multiple markets and balancing global standards with regional business requirements. - Proven ability to work closely with Marketing, GTM, Sales Operations, and technical teams, influencing priorities and driving work through to completion. - Sound judgment around consent, customer data, privacy, and operational quality. NICE TO HAVE - Experience supporting JAPAC markets, including local campaign execution and collaboration across languages and time zones. - Experience with ABM, buying-group engagement, and enterprise, developer, or startup audiences. - Familiarity with data integrations, APIs, and customer engagement or product-usage signals. - Practical experience building or improving AI-enabled workflows and automation. OpenAI is an equal opportunity employer, and we value thoughtful builders who bring curiosity, rigor, and care to complex work. If you are excited to help build effective, measurable marketing operations across JAPAC, we would love to hear from you. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe our research will eventually lead to artificial general intelligence, a system that can solve human-level problems. The Community & Culture Engagement team helps people discover, use, and advocate for OpenAI’s tools through community programs, social storytelling, creator partnerships, and cultural experiences. Our work connects OpenAI with the people and communities who bring its technology into everyday life. As the team grows across disciplines and markets, we need shared foundations that connect our work, make priorities clear, and help us deliver with speed and care. About the Role We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own Community & Culture’s integrated operating model. You will build and own the infrastructure that enables the team to operate as one and execute at a consistently high standard. You are accountable for keeping the plans funded, staffed and executable as priorities change. You will establish the shared practices, clear accountability, and reliable information that allow leaders to make sound decisions and teams to deliver on their commitments. This is a senior leadership role that combines organizational judgment with hands-on building. Working closely with Community & Culture leadership and partners across OpenAI, you will turn strategy into practical operating plans, anticipate risks, and guide decisions about where we invest and how we staff the work. You will build systems people trust and use, adapting them as priorities and the organization evolve. This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Establish and own Community and Culture’s integrated operating model. This includes overseeing and building practical tools and workflows for financial management, resourcing, and operating reviews. - Own the team’s financial operating system. In partnership with Finance, Marketing, Partnerships and Comms leads, establish a consistent approach to budgeting, forecasting, spend approvals, and reporting across central and international teams. Maintain a trusted view of planned, committed, and actual spend. Responsible for driving tradeoff decisions, investment shifts and reallocation where needed. - Establish clear governance across the team. Define decision rights, build and own approval processes, clarify program ownership and appropriate handoffs to partner teams, and create clear escalation paths across the team. - Lead resourcing and capacity planning. Translate priorities into plans for full time, freelance, and agency remits. Identify gaps in skills and capacity, develop hiring and investment recommendations, and guide leaders through tradeoffs about where to add, shift, or sequence resources. - Build and own reliable agency and vendor operations. Partner with Procurement, Legal, and Finance to establish clear processes for scopes of work, contracts, onboarding, purchase orders, and renewals. Ensure external commitments have clear owners, funding, and expectations. Guide and hold teams accountable to measurable outcomes from pilot programs. - Raise the standard of operational execution. Establish meaningful measures of forecast quality, planning reliability, capacity, and follow-through. Anticipate issues before they affect delivery and lead improvements as the team grows. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 10+ years of experience in operations, business operations, or a related discipline, including senior leadership responsibility for a complex, growing organization. - A successful track record of owning budgets, forecasts, and financial planning processes, with the judgment to help senior leaders weigh competing investments and resource needs. - Experience building governance and ways of working that have been adopted across multiple teams, with clear improvements in accountability and execution. - Experience leading workforce and capacity planning across employees, contractors, and agencies, and translating business priorities into practical staffing decisions. - Sound judgment in ambiguity. You make progress with incomplete information, adapt as priorities change, and know when a problem calls for a conversation, a decision, or a better process. - The ability to move between organizational strategy and detailed execution. You are comfortable shaping an operating model, working through a budget or staffing plan, and staying accountable through implementation. - An understanding of creative, community, marketing, or other relationship-driven teams. items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The CXR Pathway Program is a paid program that launches your career in financial services. You'll be paid while you study for your SIE, Series 7 and Series 63 licenses and learn the job through hands-on, on-the-job training. You'll build foundational knowledge and confidence alongside your cohort, and finish the program ready to become a registered broker (Registered Representative). Learn by doing, from day one. While you study, you'll be on the job supporting customers across chat, email and phone, with needs ranging from simple to complex. We demonstrate insane customer focus, and you'll learn what that looks like in practice. As a member of this team, you'll be the company's voice and will use exceptional empathy and product expertise to ensure our users feel understood and valued. Your job is not only to help our customers, but to help us learn as a company from each interaction, so that we can make our customers' experience using our products as seamless as possible. This application is for our early talent with an anticipated start date in January 2027. We are looking for recent graduates who have customer-facing experience and are interested in becoming a Registered Representative through Robinhood's licensing and training program. Location: This role is based in our Denver, CO, and Westlake, TX offices, with in-person attendance expected 5 days per week during the 6-month onboarding period. channels Ability to quickly defuse customer anxiety through exceptional customer service skills Schedule flexibility as we evolve to meet the growing demands of our customers (future shift assignment items.title: Global Procurement Analyst
items.description: We are an AI company operating at the cutting edge of the industry, growing quickly in a fast-moving environment. As we scale and prepare for a future IPO, we are building our Procurement function from the ground up. This is our first Procurement Analyst role in the company, so you will help define how we buy, not just execute it. Your passion for Procurement will help build and run our source-to-pay processes with strong internal controls, clear segregation of duties between procurement and payment, and audit-ready documentation. This is a global role: you will support stakeholders and suppliers across regions and work closely with the rest of the Procure to Pay (P2P) and Finance teams. Key Responsibilities Procurement operations Manage the end-to-end purchasing operations across all spend categories (software, cloud, professional services, hardware, facilities, and more), from requisition intake and PO issuance in Zip / Coupa. Review purchase requests for completeness, budget and policy compliance before approval. Issue and track purchase orders, and follow up with suppliers on delivery, pricing, and service levels. Support RFQ/RFP processes: gather requirements, solicit/compare bids, and document selection rationale. Support negotiations and renewals in partnership with Legal and business owners. Support requesters across time zones and regions, handling multi-currency and cross-border purchasing needs. Controls and audit readiness Help design and implement procurement policies, approval matrices (delegation of authority), and procedures aligned with IPO and audit requirements. Enforce segregation of duties between procurement (requisition, sourcing, PO creation, vendor selection) and payment (invoice processing, payment execution), in coordination with Accounts Payable and Finance. Maintain complete, organized documentation for every purchase (quotes, approvals, contracts, POs) so it is available for internal and external audits. Monitor and report on policy exceptions, such as off-contract spend, retroactive POs, and split purchases, and escalate as needed. Support internal and external audit requests and help remediate findings. Vendor management Maintain accurate vendor master data and a centralized vendor and contract repository. Run supplier onboarding, including due diligence, documentation, tax compliance validation, and conflict-of-interest checks for domestic and international suppliers. Track supplier performance and support periodic vendor reviews using AI and other tools. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world. You’ll be the senior data science leader embedded in our Core Apps product team and a strategic thought partner to its product leads. You’ll help set product direction for Claude Code and other new bets across Core Apps: bringing a point of view on where to invest, how to grow our Apps business, and how to deliver more value for our users. As a tech lead manager, you’ll also manage a small team of Product Data Scientists, setting their agenda and raising the bar for how data shapes product decisions. Core Apps, deciding where the Product Data Science team can have the most impact and what it should deprioritize Manage and develop a small team of Product Data Scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions Frame the most important and ambiguous questions facing the business, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction Define how Core Apps measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks that align teams and leadership on what matters Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Core Apps, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses Turn complex analyses into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Core Apps needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our products grow You may be a About the Role We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment. The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. The strongest candidates will have deep expertise in either electrical and mechanical systems and strong working fluency across the other discipline (e.g. controls, business acumen). Remote - travel 50% Key Responsibilities - Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure. - Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems. - Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation. - Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics. - Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning. - Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability. - Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action. - Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response. - Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards. Qualifications - 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments. - Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries. - Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team. - Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement. - Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records. - Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures. - Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, technicians, vendors, construction teams, and senior stakeholders. - Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required. - Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments. - Experience bringing new sites from construction and commissioning into steady-state operations. - Working knowledge of BMS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC, or other infrastructure monitoring and controls platforms. - Experience establishing service programs, readiness criteria, technical training, or fleet-wide reliability standards. - Relevant electrical, mechanical, HVAC, controls, safety, or trade certifications. items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role AI has the power to dramatically accelerate the pace of scientific discovery and the development of healthcare interventions. Alongside the models and tools we build for scientists, Anthropic’s life science research teams now run their own wet lab experiments. We’re hiring a life sciences patent counsel to work side-by-side with our researchers as they work to advance biomedical progress. You will manage patent strategy and filings for our life sciences research, from the first conversation with a scientist through global prosecution. You will also be our in-house expert on the patent questions, many of them new, that arise when scientists use AI as a research tool. You will partner closely with our patents lead (direct manager), the Head of IP, Research Legal, our Life Sciences Counsel, and outside counsel to design and implement a patent program that supports our researchers and partners and is aligned with the company’s mission. Responsibilities Manage patent strategy and filings for Anthropic’s life sciences research in the U.S. and internationally, including invention harvesting, filing decisions, drafting oversight, prosecution, and management of outside counsel Serve as the trusted patent advisor to our life science research teams, and design and implement scalable guidance and processes to support our fast-growing life science efforts Make inventorship determinations for AI-assisted research, and advise on inventor declarations and the duty of candor Develop claim and filing strategies across biological and chemical inventions, platform technologies, and computational methods, accounting for written description, enablement, eligibility, and obviousness Partner with Research Legal and Communications on the timing of publications, preprints, presentations, and open-source releases Advise on the patent aspects of agreements with life science and biopharma counterparties, including ownership of inventions and improvements, and support patent diligence and freedom-to-operate analyses for our research Anticipate emerging legal developments affecting AI technologies in the life science and biopharma space and provide strategic guidance to leadership Minimum qualifications Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based A degree or equivalent training in a life sciences or chemistry field (for example, molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, bioengineering, or organic chemistry) Substantial hands-on experience drafting and prosecuting U.S. life sciences patent applications, and directing foreign prosecution through local counsel Lead responsibility for a patent portfolio, including managing budget and outside or foreign counsel Experience making inventorship determinations and resolving ownership questions in multi-party research arrangements (for example, with universities and other partners) Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate legal risk into practical guidance for scientists, researchers, and business partners A low-ego, high-empathy orientation and a “doer” attitude: willing to roll up your sleeves and pitch in where needed Intense curiosity about AI and science, and a commitment to responsible AI development Preferred qualifications 10+ years of patent experience (including time as a patent agent, technical specialist, or examiner) at a law firm, a biotech or pharmaceutical company, or both, with the ability to operate independently and hit the ground running Advanced degree in a life sciences or chemistry field Experience with AI/ML companies, or with inventions at the boundary of biology and machine learning Working knowledge of how patents interact with regulatory exclusivity, trade secrets, and open science Familiarity with biosecurity, dual-use research, or export control considerations in the life sciences Experience leveraging AI to optimize their work, with a desire to work in a fast-paced, innovative environment The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. Annual Salary: $335,000 — $385,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. items.title: Consumer Product Communications Lead
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Product & Research Communications team helps people understand our technology, what it makes possible, and how to use it. We work closely with teams across the company to bring new products and research to the world, tell stories grounded in real experiences, and build trusted relationships with journalists. About the Role We’re looking for a Consumer Product Communications Lead to shape how people understand and experience ChatGPT and OpenAI’s consumer-facing products. You’ll lead product communications strategy, launches, and proactive campaigns, and manage the agency partner supporting this work. You’ll develop a clear narrative for our consumer products and bring it to life through compelling launches, useful demonstrations, and stories about how people use AI in their everyday lives. You’ll build momentum between announcements, finding fresh ways to reach new audiences while earning the trust of the people who use our products most deeply. This role calls for a hands-on communications leader with strong editorial judgment, creative ambition, and the ability to turn ideas into results. You’ll have a clear point of view, work with substantial autonomy, and build close partnerships across the company. In this role, you will: - Own the communications strategy and narrative for ChatGPT and consumer-facing products, connecting product developments to what matters to users. - Lead product launches from strategy through execution, including positioning, messaging, media outreach, spokesperson preparation, and follow-through. - Develop proactive campaigns that show how people use our products to learn, create, and solve everyday problems. - Partner closely with Product, Research, Engineering, Marketing, Design, Legal, and other communications teams to shape plans, resolve tradeoffs, and communicate accurately. - Build relationships with consumer and technology journalists, creators, and other voices who help people understand new technology. - Direct the consumer communications agency partner, setting priorities, writing clear briefs, giving useful feedback, and holding the team accountable for quality and results. - Write and edit launch materials, pitches, talking points, and other communications with a high standard for clarity, accuracy, and originality. - Anticipate questions and concerns, bring audience feedback into planning, and assess whether campaigns improve understanding and earn trust. You might thrive in this role if you: - Expressing strong perspective / conviction / confidence / love writing narrative / influence - Strong management skills - Have a strong track record leading communications for consumer technology products, including major launches and proactive campaigns. - Can turn complex product capabilities into clear, compelling stories without losing accuracy or overstating what the technology can do. - Combine strategic judgment with hands-on execution and are as comfortable developing a narrative as writing a pitch or preparing a spokesperson. - Build trusted relationships across functions, influence decisions, and help teams reach a clear direction when perspectives differ. - Bring creative ideas and strong editorial taste. You can explain why a story, demo, or campaign will resonate and make the work better through specific feedback. - Take initiative, make sound decisions independently, and stay organized in a fast-moving environment. - Have experience managing agency partners and getting excellent work from a combined internal and external team. - Understand consumer media and culture, care about the experience of early adopters and power users, and are curious about how AI is changing people’s lives. items.title: Head of Stunt Marketing
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and sports is one of our biggest categories. The marketing team is small and moves fast. We don't have a big agency on retainer or a traditional campaign calendar. What we have is a platform that sits at the intersection of sports, news, and money, and a mandate to make the world aware of it in ways that actually stick. This role exists because guerilla and stunt marketing is one of the highest-leverage things we can do, and we need a dedicated person who owns it end to end. You'll be the one watching the game, spotting the moment, and showing up with something that earns press and goes viral, not because it was planned six months out, but because you moved faster than everyone else. The person who held this role before built a real playbook here. Your job is to run it, expand it, and make it yours. This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role. You'll work closely with the marketing lead and have real autonomy, but you'll also be expected to operate independently in the field, often on short notice. If you need a lot of structure or sign-off to act, this isn't the right fit. If you thrive on finding the moment and executing before it passes, keep reading. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Identify stunt and activation concepts tied to live sports moments, news cycles, and cultural events, then pitch them fast with a clear point of view on why they'll land - Execute on-the-ground activations at stadiums, arenas, sports bars, and public venues, handling logistics, talent, materials, and timing yourself - Monitor social media and sports news in real time to spot openings for reactive content or physical activations before the moment passes - Coordinate all logistics for guerilla campaigns from concept through execution, including permits, vendors, travel, and on-site management - items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As an IP Rights Manager on the IP & Licensing team, you will own the operational backbone of how Mistral manages rights, obligations, and restrictions across the datasets we license. This role sits at the intersection of copyright, data protection, and AI, and exists because the volume and complexity of our data agreements have outgrown manual processes. You will work closely with the colleagues who negotiate our agreements commercially and legally, translating their work into systems, workflows, and databases that keep us compliant and scalable. The IP & Licensing team is responsible for all content and data licensing at Mistral. Your work will directly determine whether we can use the data we acquire, how we track what we are allowed to do with it, and whether our clients and partners stay within the rights we grant them. You will build the infrastructure that makes legal analysis repeatable, not just advisory. Your scope spans the full lifecycle of data-related agreements: clearing inbound data usage requests, codifying contract terms into structured metadata, tracking ongoing compliance obligations, and automating reporting. You will also design and run AI-powered workflows that handle contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and renewal alerts, turning legal judgment into scalable operations. What You Will Do - Clear inbound data usage requests by researching rights status, scope, obligations, and restrictions before data enters Mistral systems. - Review data-related agreements and codify their key terms into structured metadata, maintaining the team's template library and playbook alongside Legal. - Determine whether specific AI use cases are covered by third-party agreements, identify gaps, and recommend contract amendments. - Build and maintain a central database as the single source of truth for every signed data-related agreement, covering permitted uses, confidentiality, and re-use permissions. - Track ongoing compliance obligations and automate reporting, including renewal alerts and master licensing partnership administration. - Develop and run AI workflows for contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and compliance monitoring. - Verify provenance, ownership, and consents for acquired data, flagging obligations that must be tracked. - Monitor that Mistral clients and partners operate within granted rights, administering the approval system that enforces legal restrictions. What We're Looking For - A bachelor's degree in law, publishing, information science, business, or a related field. - 2 to 5 years of experience in copyright, permissions, licensing, legal operations, or contract administration, ideally in an AI, tech, or data-driven environment. - Solid working knowledge of EU and US copyright law and contract administration, with demonstrated ability to interpret contracts independently. - Strong attention to detail and discretion when handling confidential agreements. - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain legal constraints to non-lawyers. - A legal-ops mindset: you take initiative, anticipate needs through ambiguity, and think about how to operationalize legal analysis at scale. - Comfort building agentic AI workflows in a complex enterprise environment; you are an AI power user, not just a consumer. - Fluency in French, German, Spanish, or another European language is a plus, as is experience with CLM tools like Ironclad, prior work setting up AI workflows in a legal team, or contracting experience with publishing houses. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE The Field CTO role is one of Mistral's senior external technical voices; a role for someone who has earned genuine credibility in the AI field and can engage enterprise boards, CIOs, and CTOs as a peer. You will shape how strategic accounts think about their AI strategy, represent Mistral at major industry events, and publish thought leadership that reflects a real point of view on where AI is going. You will work closely with regional sales leadership across your territory and bring what you learn from executive conversations back into Mistral's product direction. This is an externally-facing, influence-driven role. The output is measured in relationships built, content published, and executive conversations that move. WHAT YOU WILL DO Executive engagement Run Mistral's Executive Briefing Center with your regional VP; a selective program for C-level stakeholders at strategic accounts. Build and sustain trusted-advisor relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and VP Engineering across your territory.
