items.title: Program Manager, Critical Harm Operations
items.description: About the Team Critical Harm Operations sits within User Safety & Risk Operations and builds enforcement systems for Frontier Risk and Material Harm that are accurate, fast, defensible, and built to scale. We turn policy intent into operational readiness, review standards, quality systems, escalation paths, automation guardrails, and durable cross-functional operating models. About the Role We are looking for an exceptional Program Manager to help build durable operating systems and run some of OpenAI’s most complex safety operations. The core need is a high-agency operator who can take an ambiguous problem, create the right structure, align cross-functional partners, and drive the work through execution. This role will move across Critical Harm priorities as needs evolve. You may step into operationalizing national security or violent-activities workflows, support wellbeing and Frontier Risk initiatives, or help scale programs such as Trusted Access. Deep domain expertise is helpful but not required; the strongest candidates will learn quickly, exercise excellent judgment, and make complex programs move. This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement by end of year. In this role, you will: - Lead strategic operational builds across priority workflows from problem statement to implemented operating model, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, success measures, and execution cadence. - Translate policy, safety, technical, legal, and operational constraints into workflows, requirements, playbooks, escalation paths, and decision-making structures that teams can execute. - Coordinate with User Ops leadership, Product Policy, Integrity, Safety Systems, i2, Legal, Product, Engineering, Support, vendors, and other partners to resolve dependencies and keep critical work moving. - Move in and out of workflows as priorities shift—standing up new programs, stabilizing operations, improving handoffs, and transitioning durable ownership to the right team. - Use operational data and frontline signals to identify bottlenecks, quality gaps, capacity needs, ownership failures, and the highest-leverage interventions. - Drive high-priority escalations and cross-functional decisions to closure, ensuring the right context, accountable owners, clear next steps, and durable follow-up. - Create the mechanisms that make programs run well: roadmaps, decision logs, status updates, risk registers, operating reviews, and crisp executive communication. - Identify where AI tools, automation, lightweight systems, or simpler workflows can improve speed, consistency, and scale while preserving appropriate human judgment. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 8+ years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, technical program management, trust and safety, support operations, risk operations, implementation, or a related field. - Experience in cybersecurity, biosecurity, or related risk and safety operations is a plus - Have a track record of taking complex, ambiguous work from problem framing through launch and scaled operation. - Are unusually organized, sharp, and execution-focused; you can manage many moving pieces without losing the few decisions that matter most. - Build trust and drive alignment across teams without direct authority, while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear. - Are technically and analytically fluent enough to reason about data flows, dashboards, tooling gaps, automation, and failure modes—even if you are not writing production code. - Communicate clearly with technical, operational, policy, and executive audiences, especially when tradeoffs are sensitive or evidence is incomplete. - Operate calmly and flexibly in a fast-moving environment, learn new domains quickly, and are comfortable handling high-severity or sensitive work. - Experience with vendor operations, QA programs, launch readiness, workflow automation, or AI-assisted operations. Nice to have: - Experience in customer support or other high-stakes scaled operations. - Deep expertise with national security, violence or other severe-harm domains. items.title: Counsel, Employment
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in advancing our mission by tackling innovative and fundamental legal issues in AI. The team includes professionals with expertise spanning technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. If you’re passionate about meaningful and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you. About the Role We are seeking an employment lawyer to help build the legal foundations for OpenAI’s next stage of growth. Working closely with our employment counsel team and colleagues across the company, you will shape practical approaches to challenging employment issues in a fast-growing AI company. This is a hands-on role for a thoughtful lawyer who enjoys variety, moves quickly, and wants to help build a strong employment legal function as the business scales. You will collaborate with experienced employment counsel on US and international employment issues, the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions, and emerging questions about AI in the workplace. A central part of your work will be turning lessons from individual matters into practical policies, guidance, and approaches that work at scale. You will also own stakeholder relationships and manage counseling matters, exercising sound judgment and taking responsibility for outcomes. You will join a bright, collaborative team that values initiative and shared learning, with opportunities to learn from senior colleagues, deepen your expertise, and take on increasingly complex matters over time. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Help shape OpenAI’s employment legal approach as the company scales, developing practical policies, playbooks, and processes that address recurring issues and support sound, timely decisions. - Collaborate with senior employment counsel and cross-functional partners on a broad range of US employment matters, including recruiting and hiring, performance management, employee conduct, leaves of absence, accommodations, and separations. - Own designated stakeholder relationships and counseling matters, providing clear, practical advice and working independently while drawing on the team’s experience and judgment as appropriate. - Advise on international employment matters and support the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions, including diligence and workforce integration, collaborating with local and specialist counsel as appropriate. - Partner on strategic projects and emerging legal questions, including the use of AI in employment and workplace practices. - Translate legal developments and lessons from your work into useful guidance, training, brown bags, and office hours for stakeholders across the company. - Manage employment disputes, administrative charges, and related matters in collaboration with colleagues and outside counsel, as appropriate. - Draft and negotiate employment documents and agreements, and identify practical ways to strengthen how the company handles employment matters as it grows. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 7+ years of relevant employment law experience at a law firm, an in-house legal team, or a combination of both, with a record of excellent work and increasing responsibility. - Have strong knowledge of US employment law, including California law, and sound judgment in advising on a broad range of workplace matters. - Analyze unfamiliar issues quickly and translate complex legal requirements into clear, practical recommendations that account for business needs and employee experience. - Enjoy building in a fast-growth environment: spotting gaps, developing practical solutions, and seeing them through to implementation. - Bring initiative, a strong work ethic, and consistent follow-through; manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work at a fast pace. - Take ownership of your work, welcome feedback, and value the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues; exercise sound judgment about when to act independently, collaborate, or escalate. - Build trusted relationships through clear communication, discretion, and empathy, and contribute to a collaborative team that shares knowledge and supports one another. - Are curious about technology, comfortable with ambiguity, and motivated by OpenAI’s mission. - Have a JD and are licensed or qualified to practice in California. Preferred Qualifications - Experience advising on international employment matters and the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions. - Experience providing AI-specific employment law advice, including advising on AI enablement, automation, and employee privacy in workplace or product contexts. items.title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure. Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations. About the Role OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing. You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits. This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders. In this role, you will: - Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions. - Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions. - Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs. - Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting. - Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits. - Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk. - Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates. - Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines. - Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs. - Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions. - Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review. - Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows. - You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Strategic Sourcing and manufacturing-partner management retain commercial negotiations; Engineering retains design and qualification authority; DC and site teams own their source inputs; Finance retains budgets, accounting, and financial approvals; Planning owns the demand baseline; SCPM owns material readiness; and OPM owns operational execution. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Significant experience in hardware product costing, cost engineering, supply chain finance, manufacturing cost analysis, or a related role supporting complex technology products. - Experience building and maintaining multi-level costed BOMs, system cost roll-ups, and lifecycle or TCO models across product development, production ramp, and sustaining operations. - Strong understanding of hardware cost drivers, including component pricing, manufacturing labor and overhead, NRE, tooling, yield, scrap, test, logistics, and service costs. - Demonstrated ability to evaluate engineering changes, second-source options, and cost-reduction opportunities using comparable scenarios and transparent assumptions. - Advanced spreadsheet and quantitative modeling skills, with disciplined data reconciliation, version control, and source traceability. - Ability to turn incomplete or changing technical and commercial inputs into defensible analysis, identify uncertainty, and drive input gaps to closure. - Strong cross-functional influence and communication skills, including concise leadership recommendations and detailed working sessions with engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and finance teams. - High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and competing priorities. Preferred Qualifications - Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, custom silicon, servers, networking, storage, or rack-scale systems. - Experience analyzing JDM, CM, or ODM cost structures and open-book manufacturing models. - Familiarity with DC and site economics, power and cooling, deployment timing, spares, and service costs in infrastructure TCO. - Experience with ERP, MRP, and PLM systems, BOM change control, and business intelligence or automation/AI tools. - A background in engineering, finance, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related analytical discipline. What Success Looks Like - Teams use a complete, current, and traceable costed BOM and system/pod baseline as the source of truth for product economics. - Platform TCO comparisons use consistent scope and assumptions, with inputs validated by their owners. - Material engineering and sourcing decisions include timely cost-impact analysis and explicit tradeoffs. - Cost variances have clear explanations, accountable owners, and recovery actions; savings and cost avoidance are validated. - Leadership receives clear recommendations, and cost-management processes scale with the complexity of the 1P hardware roadmap. items.title: Security Data Engineer
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Security at that scale runs on data, and you'll be the engineer who owns it and the systems that produce it: component-level hardware inventory and chain of custody, fed by software that runs at our sites and on hosts, and continuous control monitoring, with the posture calculations that decide what each site is cleared to run. You set the architecture, agree schemas and interfaces with the teams, operators and vendors that own the sources, build the pipelines, stores and tools, and run what you ship. The goal is security that runs itself: custody, access and evidence verified continuously from records, with tools and AI agents doing the reviews. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's compute and data center operations teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities Hardware inventory and chain of custody: own the component-level record of what hardware exists, where it is and who has handled it: the data model, the pipelines that join inventory and custody events from many source systems, change history on every record, and the tamper-evident stores behind it Tools, automation and AI agents: build the tools and agents the team runs on this data: reconciliation, audit evidence exports, custody checks. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it Custody workflows and field software: build the workflows and the site and host software that capture custody events as they happen (a receipt, a move, a data wipe, a decommission) and enforce who is authorized to record them Continuous control monitoring and posture: own the pipelines that turn check outcomes, assessment results and findings into per-control and per-site measures over time, against the compliance frameworks we and our partners are assessed against, and the posture calculation that decides what a site is cleared to run Data quality: build coverage checks, reconciliation against sources and alerts on a silent or drifting feed, so a wrong or missing record is caught the same day; own retention and access controls on the records Integration and reporting: agree schemas and interfaces with the engineers who run the security monitoring platform, and build the query surfaces and reports the team, site leads and leadership use directly Minimum qualifications Have designed and run production data systems (relational schemas, change data capture, batch or streaming pipelines and the services around them) and kept them correct: coverage measured, records reconciled against the source, alerts on silence, and a design that expects records to get corrupted or lost Have integrated with systems you did not control (inventory tools, ticketing systems, vendor APIs) and built data models that outlive any one source Have shipped software that runs outside a central service (host agents, site-local services, edge collectors) and kept it correct in the field, or built metrics a team made decisions on and defended them when challenged Have worked hands-on with data about physical assets or security controls: a hardware fleet, data center or supply chain inventory, asset custody, or the control and evidence data of a security or compliance program Read and review other people's code, and build with AI coding agents using Git and code review Own a domain end to end: set the approach, design and build it with the teams and vendors whose systems it depends on, and run it as something people use every day Write SQL and at least one general-purpose programming language well Preferred qualifications Experience with asset management, supply chain or warehouse systems where serialized tracking and custody transfer are the core problem Experience building continuous control monitoring or metrics for a security or compliance program, or producing evidence an assessor accepted, for example against NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001 or SOC 2 Experience with risk or posture scoring that combines control results, findings and other evidence into a measure people make decisions on Familiarity with data center hardware and its lifecycle from receipt to decommission, and with sites and parties you did not control: colocation, cloud or GPU cloud operators, hardware manufacturers, logistics providers Have run software on many hosts or at remote sites with versioned rollout and a way to know each copy is still reporting Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Events Designer, Business Marketing
items.description: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. Business Marketing helps organizations understand and put OpenAI’s products to work. Our creative team brings that story to life across campaigns, launches, and everyday marketing experiences. We work closely with marketing partners to make ambitious, thoughtful creative work that connects with business audiences. About the Role We’re looking for an experienced Events Designer to create memorable visual experiences across OpenAI events, live streams, and global product announcements. You’ll develop cohesive visual identities and translate them across keynote presentations, large-format screens, streaming graphics, event environments, and merchandise. Working closely with brand, marketing, events, motion, and production teams, you’ll bring strong creative thinking and hands-on design craft to every experience. In this role, you will - Design event experiences from concept to execution, including signage, wayfinding, wall graphics, apparel, merchandise, and other onsite brand applications. - Build cohesive visual systems that extend across physical environments, keynote presentations, large-format screens, and digital event touchpoints. - Create broadcast and livestream graphics, including overlays, lower thirds, titles, countdowns, and other motion-ready assets. - Storyboard and art-direct motion work in partnership with internal motion designers and external creative partners, ensuring consistency across formats. - Collaborate with producers, motion designers, video teams, artists, event planners, marketing, and product partners to translate event objectives into distinctive creative work. - Maintain and evolve OpenAI’s brand system in event contexts, creating reusable templates, documenting design decisions, and supporting the scalable execution of global events. items.title: Trading Specialist
items.location_text: Chicago, IL; Denver, CO; Lake Mary, FL; New York, NY
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Trading Operations team is responsible for ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant trade execution across all supported asset classes while protecting customers and the firm. The team partners closely with Engineering, Compliance, Customer Experience, and external market centers to maintain system stability and trading integrity during all market sessions. Robinhood has now introduced 24/7 trading and this hire will help support this new function. As a Trading Specialist, you will monitor live trading activity across overnight, extended hours, and regular market sessions while supporting the health of Robinhood’s trading infrastructure. You’ll investigate and resolve trading issues, coordinate responses to system or venue disruptions, and communicate clearly with internal teams and external partners. This role offers hands-on exposure to trading operations, risk management, and customer-impacting decisions, with meaningful opportunities for learning and career growth! This role is remote but will be tied to a local Robinhood office in New York, NY, Lake Mary, FL, Chicago, IL, or Denver, CO. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. Shifts Available: Work Schedule 1 (all times are EST): Tuesday 11:30AM - 8:30PM Thursday 11:30AM - 8:30PM Saturday 9AM - 9PM Sunday 9AM - 9PM Work Schedule 2 (all times are EST): Friday 9pm - Sat 9am (Friday overnight to Saturday) Sat 9pm - Sun 9am (Saturday overnight to Sunday) Sunday 8pm - Mon 5am (Sunday overnight to Monday) Wednesday 8pm - Thurs 5am (Wednesday overnight to Thursday) What you’ll do Execution of Written Supervisory Procedures to comply with all SEC and FINRA rules Order entry and trade execution of equity and option orders Resolution of trade inquiries Monitor trading activity, firm accounts, corporate actions, and identify and resolve problems associated with trades Monitor health of routing systems and Venues, and interact with Venues as required Coordinate response for system, trading, and communications (SEV) related issues. Engage with cross functional teams (Product, Engineering, Compliance) on product development and problem solving. What you bring Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience 3-5 years working in a broker-dealer operations/trading environment FINRA Series 7 required FINRA 57 license required Strong understanding of brokerage operation functions Self-starter with ability to work independently Strong communication and analytical skills Ability to effectively prioritize and adapt to a changing environment What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $115,000 — $135,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $101,000 — $119,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $89,000 — $105,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Physical Engineering team sits within OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. We’re exploring how frontier AI can help people design, simulate, and build better physical products—shortening development cycles, improving product performance, and expanding what engineering teams can accomplish. Our initial focus is on mechanical and electrical engineering. We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with engineering software to help engineers move from early concepts through design, simulation, and preparation for production. We operate as a small founding team within OpenAI, working directly with customers and closely with research, design, and forward deployed engineers. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide our next steps. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll help define and build the product and technical foundations of this new vertical. You’ll work across frontend experiences, backend services, and integrations to bring AI into complex engineering workflows. You’ll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with product judgment and an eye for intuitive user experiences. Working directly with engineers and design partners, you’ll identify valuable problems, prototype solutions, and develop them into reliable products. We’re particularly interested in engineers who have built CAD, CAE, simulation, or other engineering design software. You should be comfortable owning work independently, making decisions with incomplete information, and moving between product details and system architecture. This is an opportunity to shape a new product area from its earliest stages, with significant influence over what we build, how it works, and the team we become. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build and ship full-stack AI products that help mechanical and electrical engineers work through design and simulation tasks. - Own projects from customer discovery and prototyping through production deployment and iteration. - Create intuitive interfaces that help users understand, inspect, and refine complex engineering outputs. - Develop backend services, APIs, plugins, and integrations that connect OpenAI models with engineering software. - Work directly with customers to understand engineering constraints, identify valuable applications, and translate specific needs into broadly useful products. - Partner with research, design, platform, and forward deployed engineering teams to bring emerging AI capabilities into practical workflows. - Evaluate quality and reliability, using customer feedback and product evidence to understand whether we’re improving how engineers work. - Help establish the technical foundations and engineering practices of a growing team. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have independently built and shipped substantial software products, with ownership across frontend and backend systems. - Bring strong product instincts and UI judgment, especially for tools that make complex work easier to understand and perform. - Enjoy working directly with users and translating their needs into thoughtful product and technical decisions. - Can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear starting point and a working product. - Move quickly, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and stay accountable for quality after launch. - Learn unfamiliar tools and domains quickly and communicate clearly across disciplines. - Are excited about applying frontier AI to the design and development of physical products. PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE - Building CAD, CAE, simulation, electrical design, or related professional software. - Developing interactive tools for visual, spatial, or technically complex workflows. - Connecting engineering tools through APIs, plugins, or extensions. - Building AI-powered applications and evaluating their usefulness and reliability. - Taking a product from concept to production as a founder or early engineer. items.title: Site Reliability Engineer
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role We are seeking highly experienced Site Reliability Engineers (SRE) to shape the reliability, scalability and performance of our platform and customer facing applications. You will work closely with our software engineers and research teams to ensure our systems meet and exceed our internal and external customers' expectations. What You Will Do As a Site Reliability Engineer, you balance the day-to-day operations on production systems with long-term software engineering improvements to reduce operational toil and foster the reliability, availability, and performance of these systems. Operations • Design, build, and maintain scalable, highly available and fault-tolerant infrastructures to support our web services and ML workloads • Make sure our platform, inference and model training environments are always highly available and enable seamless replication of work environments across several HPC clusters • Operate systems and troubleshoot issues in production environments (interrupts, on-call responses, users admin, data extraction, infrastructure scaling, etc.) • Implement and improve monitoring, alerting, and incident response systems to ensure optimal system performance and minimize downtime • Implement and maintain workflows and tools (CI/CD, containerization, orchestration, monitoring, logging and alerting systems) for both our client-facing APIs and large training runs • Participate occasionally in on-call rotations to respond to incidents and perform root cause analysis to prevent future occurrences Development • Drive continuous improvement in infrastructure automation, deployment, and orchestration using tools like Kubernetes, Flux, Terraform • Collaborate with AI/ML researchers to develop and implement solutions that enable safe and reproducible model-training experiments • Build a cloud-agnostic platform offering an abstraction layer between science and infrastructure • Design and develop new workflows and tooling to improve to the reliability, availability and performance of our systems (automation scripts, refactoring, new API-based features, web apps, dashboards, etc.) • Collaborate with the security team to ensure infrastructure adheres to best security practices and compliance requirements • Document processes and procedures to ensure consistency and knowledge sharing across the team • Contribute to open-source projects, research publications, blog articles and conferences What We're Looking For • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field • 7+ years of experience in a DevOps/SRE role • Strong experience with cloud computing and highly available distributed systems • Exposure to site reliability issues in critical environments (issue root cause analysis, in-production troubleshooting, on-call rotations...) • Experience working against reliability KPIs (observability, alerting, SLAs) • Hands-on experience with CI/CD, containerization and orchestration tools (Docker, Kubernetes...) • Knowledge of monitoring, logging, alerting and observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack, Datadog...) • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CloudFormation • Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Go, Bash...) and knowledge of software development best practices • Strong understanding of networking, security, and system administration concepts • Excellent problem-solving and communication skills • Self-motivated and able to work well in a fast-paced startup environment Your application will be all the more interesting if you also have: • experience in an AI/ML environment • experience of high-performance computing (HPC) systems and workload managers (Slurm) • worked with modern AI-oriented solutions (Fluidstack, Coreweave, Vast...) WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.
